name: PLX-2
description: The PLX-2 was a portable missile launcher manufactured by Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc. during the Galactic Civil War. It was effective against repulsorcraft, as well as vehicles, atmospheric flying craft, fortifications, and other missiles. The PLX-2 was a lightweight shoulder-mounted launcher operated by a single soldier. The launcher housed one missile in the chamber, and a second in reserve. It could fire two separate kind of missiles rounds; "dumb" rockets and GAM guided missiles. The "dumb" rockets were fired in a line-of-sight attack, but the GAM guided missiles could be programmed to track a target. The GAM guided missile supported two tracking modes, which were selectable by a firing stud on the launcher itself. In EPR mode, the missile locked onto to IR sources such as vehicle exhaust or missile contrails. In Gravity-Activated Mode—after which the missile is named—the missile's targeting computer recorded the target's silhouette and pursued it until close enough to lock onto the gravity-wave anomalies from the target's repulsorlift. A GAM guide missile in GAM mode could track a target for forty kilometers before running out of fuel, although it could be confused by other targets and evasive maneuvers.
